question: What is the popular name for mercury(I) chloride which is used as a laboratory reagent and as a depolarizer in dry batteries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calomel.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The popular name for **mercury(I) chloride** is **Calomel.**
 
• Calomel is a **white crystalline powder** that is used as a** laboratory reagent** and as a **depolarizer **in dry batteries.
 
• It is also used in medicine as a **purgative** and as a treatment for** syphilis.**
 
• Calomel has been used historically as a **laxative** and as a treatment for various ailments, but its use has declined due to its **toxicity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phosgene** is a **toxic gas.**

 
 
• It was used as a **chemical weapon** in World War I.
 
 
 
• **Galena **is a** mineral.**
 
 
• It is a **source of lead.**
 
 
 
• **Saltpetre** is a common name for **potassium nitrate.**
 
 
• It is used in **fertilizer **and in the production of **gunpowder.**
